Issued at 300 AM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Dangerous Heat Today:

The eastern extent of an upper-level ridge extending into the 
local area will dictate daytime heat indices and storm chances.
Currently, the recent HREF has very high probabilities (over 
80%) for heat indices to reach over 100 degrees areawide with 
respectable probabilities (30-70%) for heat indices to reach 
over 105 degrees south of I-94. This is mostly due to the fact 
that the NBM has fairly high confidence (70-100%) for dewpoints 
reaching over 75 degrees for areas south of I-94. While 80
degree dewpoints are likely (30-70% NBM), resulting in heat 
indices over 110 degrees, have tempered 85 degree dewpoints from
select sites in northeast Iowa in collaboration with neighboring
forecast offices. Given the expected dangerous heat, an Extreme
Heat Warning is in effect for areas along and south of I-94. 

Storm Potential Today:

The main forecast challenge will be how convection develops 
later into the afternoon and into the evening. The ongoing
signal in CAMs is for early evening convective initiation from 
a shortwave impulse and enhancing upper-level jet streak
progressing into northern WI. The main remaining question is 
exactly how far west convective initiation occurs in lieu of 
the aforementioned upper-level ridge. Overall, confidence is 
increasing for portions of western WI at risk for storms as much
of the 00z CAMs favor convecting east of the Mississippi River.

A fairly conducive severe weather environment persists as storms
shift southeast due to stronger middle/upper-level flow in the 
recent RAP supports both MCS maintenance and/or supercells with
any discrete storms. Consequently, current confidence for both 
large hail and damaging winds as main threats, even some very 
strong wind gusts (Over 74 mph) with favorable DCAPE values over
1000 J/kg, especially should any bowing segments occur in 
linear modes. 

Should the aforementioned ridge axis advect farther east, 
convection will likely be east of the local area due to capping 
from warmer temperatures aloft. Although, the recent 00z HRRR
suggested additional storm development farther west through the
Mississippi River Valley due to propagating outflow boundaries.

Summarily, a fairly complex setup this evening and overnight
into Monday, although confidence is increasing slightly for 
storms to develop by evening across portions of west/north- 
central WI with a risk for damaging wind gusts and large hail. 
Thinking that extreme heat is high confidence (over 80%) as 
confidence for afternoon storms is lower at this point with the 
higher confidence period being more into the evening hours in 
light of the recent CAMs and when the stronger flow aloft works 
its way in. 

Heat Risk Continues Monday: 

As we head into Monday, a weak surface boundary will push into the 
area during the afternoon and evening hours which will re-establish 
northwesterly flow across the local area. As a result, expecting 
dewpoints to decrease behind this front which should keep heat 
indices tempered slightly for areas north of I-90. That being said, 
the grand ensemble (GEFS/EC/Canadian ensemble) has been fairly 
consistent with high confidence (50-70% chance) for heat indices 
over 100 degrees for areas south of I-90, thus have upgraded the
ongoing Extreme Heat Watch to an Extreme Heat Warning. Should
diurnal timing and progression of the frontal boundary affect
realized Heat Indices, these areas may require additional
amendment to an Advisory or potentially removal. Given varying 
criteria with more southern latitude forecast offices that near 
climatologically warmer thresholds, collaboration in neighboring
forecast offices persisted Extreme Heat Watch.

Monday Storm Potential: 

Some storms cannot be ruled out (10-30% chance) in west- 
central WI for Monday morning and into the afternoon which may 
contain some severe threat, however this window would be 
relatively brief as the the main forcing with the associated 
shortwave pushes east of the region fairly quickly. Would also 
need to watch later into the afternoon with the aforementioned 
weak boundary that pushes through which could initiate storms as
well which would be accompanied with a severe threat as the 
aforementioned upper-level jet streak remains in place. 

Tuesday-Saturday: Warm Temperatures Continue with Storm Chances

The ridge shifts westward just enough and northwest flow remains in 
place. Both of these will mean temperatures cool down slightly, into 
the mid to upper 80s but it also means that the 70F dewpoints would 
be less likely to occur. Heat indices will also stay in the 80s to 
around 90F. With this flow pattern, ensemble guidance has low 
precipitation chances through midweek with better chances as we head 
towards the weekend. Another thing to note is that given the 
northwest flow pattern, we will have to watch for any waves that 
ride around the ridge as these would impact portions of the Upper 
Midwest.
